added: This chapter states how the loop runs a model through time.
It takes the execution order (§5.3) and the compiled executor (§9.7) as given.

§10.1 covers loop ownership and the loop's two units; §10.2 the stepper seam; §10.3 signal-table consistency; §10.4 localization mechanics; §10.5 multi-rate tick scheduling; §10.6 event iteration at boundaries; and §10.7 real-time pacing.
This section defines the simulation loop's two units, lists its six activities and states who writes the loop.
`t` is an event's crossing instant inside a step, bracketed by root-finding (§10.4).
D-017 records the rejected foreign-loop alternative.
- The seam carries what a backend needs across a frame top through a checkpoint hook, empty for a single-step method.
A checkpoint is the executor's state at a frame top (§12.6, D-274).
The Flight.jl evidence behind these claims lives in section 5 of `companions/flight_case_studies.md`.
